entries.name: box-nested-unsized-softfork-reject#0
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The nested box's tree is unsized, 00 d1 fd, whose unknown opcode fd fails rule 1002. Unsized, the nested tree turns that ValidationException into a SerializerException ('ErgoTree serialized without size bit.'), which does not degrade the outer tree either: the JVM rejects. An impl that degrades the outer tree on any nested failure accepts it: the over-accept.

entries.name: box-nested-sized-softfork-accept#1
entries.description: The twin: A bare box whose nested tree is the same, size-flagged (08 02 d1 fd). It degrades on its own, so the outer tree parses. Round-trip identity.

entries.name: box-nested-rule-1012-degrade-accept#2
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The nested box's tree header is 01, a v1 tree without the size bit. CheckHeaderSizeBit (rule 1012, ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:219) runs before the nested tree's own handler (:145), so its ValidationException reaches the outer tree, which degrades. Round-trip identity. An impl that treats it as a hard error rejects: the over-reject.

entries.name: box-nested-rule-1012-unsized-outer-reject#3
entries.description: The twin: A bare box whose outer tree is the same but unsized (10): the ValidationException cannot degrade it, so the JVM rejects.

entries.name: box-nested-rule-1019-degrade-accept#4
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The outer tree is v3 (1b), and the nested box's R4 is Option[Int] Some(1) (28 01 02): well-formed data that CheckV6Type (rule 1019, ErgoBoxCandidate.scala:232) refuses in a register. The ValidationException degrades the outer tree. Round-trip identity.

entries.name: box-nested-option-register-unsized-outer-reject#5
entries.description: The twin: A bare box whose outer tree is unsized v0 (10). There the Option data fails rule 1009 (no Option data below tree v3), and unsized, the outer tree cannot degrade: the JVM rejects.

entries.name: box-nested-sheader-register-v1-reject#6
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The outer tree is v1 (19), and the nested box's R4 is an SHeader (68, then a 215-byte header). Below tree v3 there is no data serializer for SHeader, a SerializerException, not a ValidationException: the size flag does not help and the JVM rejects.

entries.name: box-nested-sheader-register-v3-degrade-accept#7
entries.description: The twin: A bare box whose outer tree is v3 (1b): the SHeader parses, then rule 1019 refuses it in a register, and the outer tree degrades. Round-trip identity.

entries.name: box-nested-seven-registers-r4-degrade-accept#8
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The outer tree is v3, and the nested box declares 7 registers, R4 = Option[Int] Some(1), then 6 × Int 1. The registers are read in order and R4 fails rule 1019 before the seventh register's missing id is ever looked up (which would reject, see tree_degrade_gate #17), so the outer tree degrades. Round-trip identity. An impl that checks the register count first rejects.

entries.name: box-nested-unsized-int-root-reject#9
entries.description: A bare box whose size-flagged, segregated tree has constant 0 = a Box, constant 1 = SigmaProp(true) and the body ConstantPlaceholder(1). The nested box's tree is unsized, 00 04 02, whose root is Int 1: rule 1001 (the root must be a SigmaProp, ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:174) fails in the nested tree. Unsized, the nested tree turns that ValidationException into a SerializerException ('ErgoTree serialized without size bit.'), as #0 does for rule 1002, so the outer tree does not degrade: the JVM rejects. An impl that degrades the outer tree accepts it: the over-accept.

entries.name: box-nested-sized-int-root-accept#10
entries.description: The twin: A bare box whose nested tree is the same, size-flagged (08 02 04 02). Rule 1001 degrades it on its own, so the outer tree parses. Round-trip identity.
